reason: The passage contains several regular (non-elite) people characters who exercise agency. Most notably, an anonymous archer draws his bow and strikes King Ahab between the joints of his armor, directly causing the king's death and altering the course of events (וְאִ֗ישׁ מָשַׁ֤ךְ בַּקֶּ֙שֶׁת֙ לְתֻמּ֔וֹ וַיַּכֶּה֙ אֶת־ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל). Additionally, the chariot commanders (שָׂרֵי הָרֶ֔כֶב) make tactical decisions about whom to pursue, servants/attendants are tasked with fetching Micaiah, and the 400 prophets collectively advise on the war. These ordinary people demonstrate real agency through their choices and actions that affect the narrative outcome.
